### **RYR1** (Ryanodine Receptor 1) — Primary Gene

RYR1 is the most strongly and most frequently implicated gene in **Malignant Hyperthermia Susceptibility (MHS)**. It encodes the skeletal muscle ryanodine receptor responsible for sarcoplasmic calcium release.

- **Guideline status:** CPIC and EMHG (European MH Group) both classify RYR1 variants as **Level A/1A evidence** for MH susceptibility.
- Pathogenic RYR1 variants → uncontrolled calcium release when exposed to **volatile anesthetic agents** (halothane, sevoflurane, desflurane, isoflurane) or **succinylcholine**.
- Inheritance is typically **autosomal dominant**.

### **CACNA1S** (α1S subunit of L-type voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channel) — Secondary Gene

A smaller subset (~1%) of MH families carry pathogenic **CACNA1S** variants, also with Level 1A evidence in CPIC guidelines.

### Clinical Bottom Line

| RYR1 | ~70% | CPIC 1A |

## CFTR — the definitive Cystic Fibrosis gene

> ⚠️ No graph context was retrieved for this query. The answer below draws on established pharmacogenomic knowledge, not the local knowledge graph.

**CFTR** (*Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Conductance Regulator*, chromosome 7q31.2) is the sole gene causally responsible for Cystic Fibrosis and is the target of all approved CFTR modulator therapies.

### Pharmacogenomic relevance

| Variant class | Example alleles | Modulator response |
|---|---|---|
| Gating (Class III) | G551D | Ivacaftor (potentiator) — high efficacy |
| Processing (Class II) | F508del (most common) | Elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (Trikafta) |
| Minimal function | ~170 loss-of-function alleles | May qualify for Trikafta per FDA label |

CPIC and PharmGKB classify CFTR variant-guided dosing of ivacaftor as **Level 1A evidence** — the strongest tier — because genotype directly predicts whether the drug will have any therapeutic effect. Prescribing ivacaftor to a patient without a gating/residual-function variant provides no benefit.

### Bottom line
**CFTR** is the only gene relevant here; there are no modifier-gene guidelines at the 1A/1B level for CF pharmacotherapy at this time.

### **IFNL3** (formerly *IL28B*) — Level 1A Evidence

**IFNL3** (Interferon Lambda 3, chromosome 19q13) is the gene with the strongest pharmacogenomic guideline association for chronic HCV:

- **Key variant:** rs12979860 (C/T)
  - **CC genotype** → ~2× higher sustained virologic response (SVR) to peginterferon-α + ribavirin

- **CPIC Guideline:** Provides actionable prescribing guidance for peginterferon/ribavirin based on IFNL3 diplotype [PMID:22677960]
- **PharmGKB:** Annotated as **Level 1A** (highest evidence tier)

### Clinical Caveat
With the widespread adoption of **direct-acting antivirals (DAAs)** — sofosbuvir, ledipasvir, etc. — IFNL3 genotyping has become largely **obsolete in practice**, as DAA regimens achieve >95% SVR regardless of IFNL3 status.

### Summary
| Gene | Variant | Evidence | Context |
|------|---------|----------|---------|
| *IFNL3* | rs12979860 | Level 1A | Peginterferon/ribavirin response |

For current HCV treatment (DAA era), IFNL3 testing is not routinely recommended.

**CFTR** (*Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane conductance Regulator*, chromosome 7q31.2) is the sole monogenic driver of Cystic Fibrosis and the central pharmacogenomic target.

### Why CFTR dominates the guidelines

| Aspect | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Disease cause** | Loss-of-function variants in *CFTR* are necessary and sufficient for CF |

### Clinical bottom line
Genotyping *CFTR* is **required** before prescribing modulators — a patient with no eligible mutation will not respond to these therapies. This makes *CFTR* one of the clearest examples of mandatory pharmacogenomic testing in any disease area.
